Manchester, John Rylands Library, MS Latin 155

div.head: Hn 7.7b
div.ab: Si uterque neccessario desit, prepositus et sacerdos et IIII de melioribus uille assint pro omnibus qui nominatim non erunt ad placitum submoniti.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 553 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: Vielleicht beruht der Satz auf uns verlorenem Erlass Heinrichs I. Vgl. Gl Vertretung 8. 9a. Das Dorf (s. d. Gl 8d) gibt bereits 1086 der Domesday-Enquête Information und haftet für Murdrum (s. d. Gl 11c). Vgl. Vinogradoff Villainage 189. 193. 218. 446; Pol Mai I 595

Perhaps the sentence rests on an enactment of Henry I that is lost to us. Cf. Gl Vertretung 8. 9a. The village (see that word in Gl 8d) already gives information to the Domesday inquest in 1086 and is liable for murdrum (see that word in Gl 11c). Cf. Vinogradoff Villainage 189. 193. 218. 446; Pol Mai I 595

div.ab: If both are of necessity absent, let the reeve and the priest and four of the better men of the vill be present for all who have not been summoned by name to the plea.
